minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to seek the originally estimated borrowing figure for Marshall Park at the Nov 12 special town meeting, despite a funding gap.
minutes.summary: The commission reviewed updated Marshall Park cost estimates that exceed the funds available for Phase One, and discussed risks to two reimbursement grants if scope is cut. A motion to put the 5.2 million figure in the warrant article was moved and seconded, and a roll call was taken with four ayes. The chair will contact the park grant administrators and poll members about an extra meeting before town meeting.

votes.motion: Move forward with the 5.2 million figure in the warrant article for Marshall Park borrowing.
votes.outcome: passed 4-0 (roll call: Karen, Colleen, Chris, chair, all aye)

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair walked through earlier appropriations for conceptual design, survey and schematics and what has been spent, leaving a remainder.

budget_items.topic: ARPA and park grant funds available
budget_items.what_was_said: Selectmen allocated ARPA funds to the project, and a park grant was added to the remaining design funds to get the total available.

budget_items.topic: Owner's project manager and design contracts
budget_items.what_was_said: Not-to-exceed contracts for the OPM and the design firm for Phase One were deducted, leaving funds for Phase One construction.
The updated estimate came in well above the funds available, so value engineering continues and some items are pushed to Phase Two, which also escalated.

budget_items.topic: Borrowing ceiling from interim town manager
budget_items.what_was_said: The interim town manager advised asking for no more than the earlier estimate; the borrowing would sit within the operating budget, replacing retiring debt, not a debt exclusion.
The grant supports Phase Two work and was based on the January cost estimate; there is a risk grants are lost if scope is reduced.
Losing the park grant would leave little for Phase One.
The chair wants the Phase One estimate brought down to the funds known to be available before proceeding; a possible ADA playground grant is not assumed.

decisions.decision: Consensus to submit the 5.2 million figure to the town manager by the 15th, keeping flexibility to amend or pass over the article later.
Chair will contact the park grant administrators around Monday and email members an FYI before the next meeting.
Chair will email members tomorrow to find a date for an additional meeting between Oct 23 and the Nov 12 special town meeting; regular meeting remains Oct 23.
Chair offered to step aside so another member can attend the Thursday design team Zoom meetings; minutes of those will be shared.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted 4-0 by roll call to put the originally estimated borrowing figure for Marshall Park in the warrant article.
The commission agreed to submit that figure to the town manager by the 15th, keeping the option to amend or pass over the article later.
Updated Phase One cost estimates came in well above the funds available, so value engineering continues and some items move to Phase Two.
Members discussed a risk that two reimbursement grants could be lost if the project scope is cut.
The chair will contact the park grant administrators and email members, and will poll them for an extra meeting before the Nov 12 special town meeting.

why_it_matters: The borrowing figure is expected to go to voters at the Nov 12 special town meeting, so residents may be asked to authorize debt for a park whose Phase One cost still exceeds the money in hand.

The interim town manager's advice, as the minutes record it, was that the borrowing would sit within the operating budget and replace retiring debt rather than be a debt exclusion, so it would not be a separate vote to raise taxes above the levy limit.
Cutting scope to close the gap could put the grant reimbursements at risk, which is a mechanism that could leave more of the cost to the town.
